Grace, Survival, and Resilience: Giving Thanks for the Life of Chief Kola Karim, the Agbaoye of Ibadanland

​By Dare Adelekan 

​In the journey of life, wealth, status, and titles can shield a person from many of society's storms, but they offer no immunity against the unpredictable forces of nature and mechanics. Recently, the Nigerian business community and the traditional landscape of Yorubaland were thrown into a moment of profound anxiety, quickly replaced by immense thanksgiving, following a terrifying mid-air incident involving a private aircraft linked to the renowned industrialist and Agbaoye of Ibadanland, Mr. Kola Karim. To God be the glory, the harrowing event ended in praise rather than tragedy, reminding everyone of the fragility of life and the supreme grace of the Almighty.

​A Close Shave in the Skies of Abuja

​The incident, which sent shockwaves through the aviation and public sectors, occurred when an aircraft connected to the Shoreline Energy boss experienced a rare and dangerous structural failure—losing its door mid-flight shortly after taking off from Abuja en route to Lagos. Flying thousands of feet in the air, a situation of that magnitude spells instant disaster in standard aviation terms. Yet, through extraordinary pilot professionalism, quick-thinking crew coordination, and divine intervention, the flight managed to squawk a Mayday call and execute a safe emergency landing back at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. 
​When news broke of the miraculous survival of those on board, sympathizers and well-wishers across the country let out a collective sigh of relief. Indeed, we must thank God for preserving his life and the lives of everyone on board.

​A Pillar of Industry and Tradition

​Beyond his corporate identity as a titan in energy, infrastructure, and international business as the head of Shoreline Energy International, Chief Kola Karim holds a revered traditional stool as the Agbaoye of Ibadanland. He is a leader who blends modern corporate sagacity with deep-rooted cultural heritage. 
​As Agbaoye, he is not only a prominent ambassador of Ibadan kingdom's rich values of resilience, bravery, and integrity, but he is also a key contributor to national economic development. Men of his caliber carry immense responsibilities—employing hundreds, driving investments, and shaping key sectors of the African economy. Losing such a dynamic figure would have created a monumental vacuum, making his miraculous survival a blessing not just to his immediate family, but to the nation at large.

​Conclusion

​The miraculous escape from the jaws of tragedy serves as a poignant reminder to stay humble and always return all glory to God, who holds the breath of all men in His hands. As the Agbaoye of Ibadanland continues his invaluable service to humanity, commerce, and tradition, this brush with mortality only reinforces the depth of grace surrounding his life. We join family, friends, associates, and the good people of Ibadanland in shouting a resounding Alhamdulillahi / E se Olohun for sparing his life. May his days be long, and may divine protection continually envelop him and his endeavors.@kolaKarim

text:
"With thee is the fountain of life."  Psalm 36:9 

There are times in our spiritual experience when human counsel or sympathy, or religious ordinances, fail to comfort or help us. Why does our gracious God permit this? Perhaps it is because we have been living too much without him, and he therefore takes away everything upon which we have been in the habit of depending, that he may drive us to himself. 

It is a blessed thing to live at the fountain head. 

While our skin-bottles are full, we are content, like Hagar and Ishmael, to go into the wilderness; but when those are dry, nothing will serve us but "Thou God seest me." We are like the prodigal, we love the swine-troughs and forget our Father's house. 

Remember, we can make swine-troughs and husks even out of the forms of religion; they are blessed things, but we may put them in God's place, and then they are of no value. Anything becomes an idol when it keeps us away from God: even the brazen serpent is to be despised as "Nehushtan," if we worship it instead of God. 

Genesis 6:6

[6] And the LORD regretted that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.

Job 13:23

    [23] How many are my iniquities and my sins?
        Make me know my transgression and my sin.

The prodigal was never safer than when he was driven to his father's bosom, because he could find sustenance nowhere else. Our Lord favours us with a famine in the land that it may make us seek after himself the more. The best position for a Christian is living wholly and directly on God's grace—still abiding where he stood at first—"Having nothing, and yet possessing all things." 

Revelation 3:3

[3] Remember, then, what you received and heard. Keep it, and repent. If you will not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come against you.

Let us never for a moment think that our standing is in our sanctification, our mortification, our graces, or our feelings, but know that because Christ offered a full atonement, therefore we are saved; for we are complete in him. Having nothing of our own to trust to, but resting upon the merits of Jesus—his passion and holy life furnish us with the only sure ground of confidence. 

Proverbs 17:9

    [9] 
    Whoever covers an offense seeks love,
        but he who repeats a matter separates close friends.

Psalm 97:11

    [11] Light is sown for the righteous,
        and joy for the upright in heart.

Psalm 100:1

    [1] Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth!

Beloved, when we are brought to a thirsting condition, we are sure to turn to the fountain of life with eagerness.

Philippians 3:3

[3] For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh—
